name: Political instability
value: No G20 collapse; Indonesia wiretap row grows
summary: Indonesian MPs questioned the police chief on 11 Nov over wiretapping of President Prabowo; no G20 government collapse
state: Indonesian lawmakers questioned the national police chief on 11 Nov over alleged illegal wiretapping of President Prabowo by senior officers, and he said the tapping extended to many others (ABC News, carrying AP). Analysts describe the case as a political showdown between Prabowo and allies of former president Joko Widodo (Foreign Policy, 11 Nov). The government is not at risk of collapse, and no G20 coup, contested election or government collapse was found in the past month as of 12 Nov.
for_you: No direct effect for most readers. Travellers to Indonesia can check FCDO travel advice for current local conditions.
rubric_hit: No G20 government collapse, contested election or coup in the past month (Normal)

sources.title: ABC News (AP) — Lawmakers question police chief about wiretaps alleged to target President Prabowo

why: Coups, contested elections and constitutional crises in large economies unsettle markets, alliances and policy.
drivers: Elections, government collapses, coups, emergency rule, mass protest movements.

rubric.alert: Coup or constitutional crisis in a G20 country, or deadly unrest threatening a G20 government.
rubric.watch: Government collapse or contested election in a G20 country, or a coup anywhere.
rubric.normal: No G20 government collapse, contested election or coup in the past month.
